image_description: A close-up underwater shot of a Rock Beauty angelfish (Holocanthus tricolor) swimming against a textured red coral background. The fish displays the characteristic black anterior body and golden-yellow posterior body/tail. The face appears slightly distorted with an open mouth, and there is a thin, isolated yellow appendage hanging from the ventral side.

artifact_observations.reasoning: A thin, needle-like yellow appendage hangs down from the belly area. This does not correspond to any known anatomical feature of a Rock Beauty (which has paired pelvic fins, not a single central spike). It suggests a fusion error or hallucinated limb.

The facial texture is overly smooth and plastic-like compared to the rest of the body. The color is incorrectly greenish-yellow instead of black, indicating a failure in attribute binding for the head region.
The mouth lacks clear definition, appearing as a smeared hole rather than a structured biological feature.
